```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

In this vignette we present all available options for the choice of the prior and Monte Carlo rule in `housepi`. 
Parameter definitions are associated as shown in the [Walkthrough](walkthrough.html).

To perform the sampling we consider the "blank" model, i. e. a data independent template model, with loglikelihood always equal to zero.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# create an instance of the blank model
hmc <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("blank")
```

## Continuos Priors

In order to see the list of available distributions present in `housepi`, just use the function `available_distributions`.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# available distributions in housepi
available_distributions <- c("unif", "norm", "lnorm", "gamma", 
                             "weibull", "rayleigh", "exp")

# add a parameter definition for each available distribution
for (distr_name in available_distributions) {
  hmc$add_param(name = distr_name, prior = distr_name)
}
```

Here we associated definitions of parameters to infer with default arguments and default proposer rules (Gibbs sampling). 
 
```{r, eval = TRUE}
# perform the sampling with the inference command
# note: since loglikelihood is 0, posterior and prior sampling are equal
hmc$infer()

# density plot of the traces (w\o loglikelihood)
# option loglikelihood = FALSE avoids to export loglikelihood
lattice::densityplot(hmc$export_traces(loglikelihood = FALSE))
```

### How to Discretize Continuos Priors

Previous continuous priors can be chosen to be discretized simply by adding the flag `discrete = TRUE`.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# drop all current definitions
hmc$drop_all()

# add a parameter definition for each available distribution
for (distr_name in available_distributions) {
  hmc$add_param(name = distr_name, prior = distr_name, discrete = TRUE)
}

# perform the sampling 
hmc$infer()

# plot the histograms
coda::densplot(hmc$export_traces(FALSE), right=FALSE)
```

### Provide a Custom Range

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# add list of parameter definitions
# option 'append = FALSE' drop previous definitions
hmc$load_param_list(
  list(
    default = list(prior = "norm"),
    below = list(prior = "norm", min = -1),
    above = list(prior = "norm", max = 1),
    both = list(prior = "norm", min = -1, max = 1)
  ), append = FALSE)
hmc$infer()

lattice::densityplot(hmc$export_traces(FALSE))
```

## Discrete Priors

Not available yet.

## MCMC Proposer Rules

```{r, eval = TRUE}
hmc$drop_all()

# available proposer rules in housepi
available_proposer_rules <- c("gibbs", "unif", "norm", "lnorm")

# add a parameter definition for each available proposer rule
for (rule_name in available_proposer_rules) {
  hmc$add_param(name = paste("rule", rule_name), 
                prior = "norm", rule = rule_name)
}

hmc$infer()

lattice::xyplot(hmc$export_traces(FALSE))

lattice::densityplot(hmc$export_traces(FALSE))
```

Note that the proposer rule "lnorm" does not fit the case of negative values as it's here visible.

## Augmented Variables

```{r}
# with model (default Gibbs rule)
hmc$drop_all()$add_augm(name = "move_1", model = "norm")
lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer()$export_traces())

# w\o model random walk (default Gibbs rule)
hmc$drop_all()$add_augm(name = "move_2", value = 0, rule = "norm")
lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer()$export_traces())

# w\o model fixed  walk (default Gibbs rule)
hmc$drop_all()$add_augm(name = "move_3", rule_from = 0, rule = "norm")

lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer()$export_traces())

```
